rules.heading: # CLAUDE.md — noahjefferson (the personal hub)

rules.says: This repo inherits the Universal App Doctrine in DOCTRINE.md (product values, taste, accessibility, honesty, verification, release discipline, licensing, privacy, the AskUserQuestion ban, the repo-metadata confirm rule) as the single source of truth for all the owner's apps, and where CLAUDE.md overlaps it the Doctrine wins.
rules.live_quote: This is the SINGLE source of truth for the rules that are the same everywhere.
rules.missing: The hub's CLAUDE.md no longer says this repo inherits the Doctrine, no longer lists what it covers, and no longer says the Doctrine wins over it; CLAUDE.md:29 only names DOCTRINE.md as 'the standing rules in full'.

rules.heading: # CLAUDE.md — noahjefferson (the personal hub)
rules.quote: Where anything below overlaps the Doctrine, the Doctrine wins. This file keeps only what is specific to this repo.
rules.says: This file holds only what is specific to this repo, and any overlap with the Doctrine is resolved in the Doctrine's favour.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: ONLY NOAH DECIDES WHAT GOES ON THE HUB — AND THAT BINDS PAGES, NOT JUST APPS.
rules.says: Only the owner decides what goes on the hub, and this binds pages as well as apps, so a session must not add or keep a page such as a planning walk or an essay (both removed 2026-09-03) that nobody asked for, and the hub's foot stays at one link.
rules.live_quote: Only the owner decides what appears on the hub's public pages, so a session adds, removes, proposes or mentions no app there unless the owner has named it.
rules.missing: That the rule binds pages that are not apps (a planning walk, an essay nobody asked for), that a session must not add or keep such a page, and that the hub's foot stays at one link.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: Adding an app here is advertising it under the owner's name.
rules.says: Adding an app to the hub is advertising it under the owner's name, and onboarding documentation for a sibling app must not be built on the hub where it cannot ship in that app's release, is untested, and goes stale.
rules.live_quote: putting an app in it is ADVERTISING it under the owner's name.
rules.missing: That a sibling app's onboarding documentation must not be built on the hub, where it cannot ship in that app's release, is untested and goes stale.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A session adds one only when the owner NAMES it — not because it is finished, not because it is already live, not because §13.6 says a repo gets wired in
rules.says: A session adds an app to the hub only when the owner names it, not because it is finished, already live, wired in per §13.6, or because its absence looks like an oversight.
rules.live_quote: A session adds an app to the hub only when the owner NAMES that app. Not when the app is finished, not when a gate is green, not when a doctrine section says a repo should be wired in, not when the app is already live ..., and not when its absence looks like an oversight

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: It binds proposing and restoring and *mentioning an unlisted app as a candidate*, which is the one that feels safe and is not.
rules.says: The only-the-owner-names-it rule also binds proposing an app, restoring one, and mentioning an unlisted app as a candidate.
rules.live_quote: **This binds four moves, not one.** Adding an app; proposing one; restoring one ...; and mentioning an unlisted app as something that could be added.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: Every deployed surface counts, not just the front page: the noscript list, the accessibility statement's app list, tiles, icons. Removal is the owner's call too.
rules.says: The rule applies to every deployed surface (front page, noscript list, accessibility statement's app list, tiles, icons), and removing an app is also the owner's call.
rules.live_quote: **It covers every surface the hub deploys** ... the noscript list, the shared accessibility statement's app list, tiles, icons ... / **Removal is the owner's call too**

rules.heading: The rules that get broken anyway
rules.quote: (Doctrine §0c — on being told this rule was nowhere in this file, the owner was right that it should not have needed to be
rules.says: A rule that is relied on should already be written in this loaded file and not need to be told to a session; a rule needed in practice belongs here.
rules.live_quote: On being told this rule was nowhere in this file, the owner was right that it should not have needed to be
rules.missing: The general principle that any rule the owner relies on belongs in the loaded instruction file and should not need telling; live text says it only about the hub-contents rule, inside never.md.
